To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

delaying spraying sugar plants with yeast extract (6 g/liter) and boron (200 mg/liter) from 75 up 90 days after sowing resulted in a gradual and significant increase in all yield components and sugar beet juice quality parameters, root and sugar yield/fad.
foliar spraying of sugar beet plants with boron and yeast extract at the rates of 200 mg and 6 g/l, respectively after 90 days of sowing is recommended for sandy soils.

foliar spraying sugar beets with yeast extract and/or boron after 75 days from sowing was not effective to improve sugar beet productivity and juice quality under sandy soil conditions, whereas spraying sugar beets after 90 days was effective to improve sugar beets productivity and juice quality, and the best results were obtained as a results of foliar application of 6 g yeast and 200 mg B/liter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of different foliar spraying times, yeast extract and borons levels on productivity and quality parameters of sugar beet.
the effect of folier spraying with yeast extract and Boron on productivity and sugar quality of sugar beet.

the effect of different times of foliar spraying sugar plants with yeast extract (after 75 or 90 days from planting) at different levels of foliar spraying with this extract (0, 2, 6 g/l) and at different levels of boron foliar spraying (0, 100, 200 mg/l) on the growth and yield of sugar beet plants under sandy soil conditions at Kalabsh farm, Dakahlia Governor, Egypt.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spraying sugar beet with yeast extract and/or boron is a good practice to maximize the productivity and quality of the crop.

foliar spraying sugar plants with yeast extract after 90 days of sowing at the rate of (6 g yeast/litre), with boron (200 mg/litre), resulted in the highest root fresh and dry weights (planted), root dimensions, sucrose and purity percentages, root and total sugar yields/fad., as well as the highest values of all juice quality parameters and the lowest values of sodium, K and amino nitrogen percentages of juice.

foliar spraying sugar beets with yeast extract and/or boron at the recommended rates and times would improve sugar beet productivity and juice quality parameters under the environmental conditions in sandy soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

spraying sugar beet with yeast extract and B at the rate of (6 g and 200 mg/liter) after 90 days of sowing would be the most suitable time and rate to maximize sugar beet production and juice quality under sandy soils.

foliar spraying of sugar beet plants with a mixture of yeast extract and B resulted in significant increases in root and sugar yields and quality parameters of root juice as compared to control treatment (no spraying).
foliar spraying sugar beets with yeast extract and boric acid
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of yeast extract and foliar application with boron at 90 days after planting and 6 g of yeast extract and 100 mg of boron/liter can be used to improve the quality and yield of sugar beet.
the foliar application of yeast extract and/or boron can improve the productivity and quality of the sugar beet plants under the sandy soil conditions.
foliar application of boron and yeast extract at the right time, rate and concentration can be used as an effective strategy to increase the productivity and quality of beet plants.
